You, Lord of the lords of gods — to whom do you offer folded hands? You are the giver of the fruit of merit of salutations and the like, Maheshvara.
naradapuran:78:199	Who is the giver of fruit to you, worthy of homage? Who is greater than you? Tell me. Hearing that, Shankara said to the God of gods, Janardana:

I meditate on nothing, Govinda; I bow to nothing. But this is shown by me, Hari, to set unbelieving creatures in motion;
naradapuran:78:201	otherwise sinners would act wrongly. Therefore all this was done by me for the benefit of the world.
Saying "Om", Hari bowed to him and remained. Then the divine sages came to Gautama's house.
All of them then worshipped the God of gods, the trident-bearer. The god sat singing with Hanuman, O lord of sages.
All of them then chanted the five-syllable great knowledge. Hara joined the two gods, taking Hanuman's hand.
The two, god and goddess, sat on one couch, and Hanuman and Tumburu and others sat singing.
The Supreme Lord made various amorous sports. Calling Parvati, Isha said these words:
I shall arrange your hair-knot; come before me, auspicious one. The Goddess said: "That is not fitting; for women, service to the husband
in doing the hair would bring on other troubles. In arranging hair, O God, I do not wish all the truth (to be told).
When the tying is done, afterward wiping the shoulders and edge; then, joined to the last, wiping the hair-flowers and so on,
while this goes on, if the great ones come, what answer shall be given by you, O one praised by gods and others?
If they do not come, Lord, my fear will vanish." Even as she spoke, Shankara drew her by the hand,
placed her on his thighs, loosened her hair-band, parted the hair with both hands and with nails,
made the hair-knot with the Parijata garland given by Vishnu on her hair, and also the garland in his hand;
taking a jasmine garland, he tied it on the hair-band; and Maheshvara took the wish-tree flower garland given by Brahma,
placing it on Parvati's garment, richly and secretly fragrant. The Lord then wiped what clung to her shoulder and back.
Her waist-cord slipping, and her garment-wrap sliding down, "What is this, Goddess?" he said, and tied the waist-knot.
This is your nose-ornament, I tell you truly. Then Shiva, daughter of the mountain, smiled and said to Shambhu:

Why do you revile the God of gods, the Lord of the world? Your wretched life, O good one, is surely not dear for want of restraint.
naradapuran:78:224	Where Isha is reviled, O good one, there for us is the vow of death. Saying so, Hari went with his nails to cut off her head.
Maheshvara, seizing his hand, said: "Do not be rash. All of Parvati's speech is dear to me, not displeasing.
Whatever you wish to do displeasing to me, Hrishikesha..." Saying "Om", the Lord Hari became silent.
Then Hanuman made this petition to the God: "I ask for my vow of worship, free of desire,
and I would go for worship; you should permit me." Hearing that, the god Shankara smiled and said to the Lord of monkeys:
Whose worship? Where is the worship? What flower, what leaf? Say: who is the teacher, what is your mantra, what is the worship like?
When Ishvara spoke so, Hanuman, skilled in conduct, trembling in all limbs, began to praise him thus:

Homage to the great god Shankara of immeasurable self; to the source of yoga, the giver of yoga, the teacher of yogis, homage.
naradapuran:78:232	To the god reached by yoga, the lord of the knowers; to the lord of the Vedas, the lord of the gods, homage to you.
naradapuran:78:233	To meditation, to the one reached by meditation, to the teacher of meditators; O eight-formed, homage to you; to the lord of beings (pashupati), homage.
naradapuran:78:234	To the three-eyed, whose eyes are moon, sun and fire; to you who love the bhringaraja, thorn-apple and drona flowers,
naradapuran:78:235	who love brihati, areca, punnaga, champaka and the like: homage to you, homage, again and again homage.
Shiva and Hari said: "Do not fear; tell me everything." Then Hanuman, free of fear, skilled in speech, said:

The worship of the Shiva-linga is to be done by one whose body is dusted with ash, with the flowers and other materials gathered by day.
naradapuran:78:238	Lord, I shall tell the auspicious rule of worshipping Shiva. When evening comes, one should bathe without wetting the head.
naradapuran:78:239	Wearing washed dry clothes, sipping water three times with focused mind, then taking ash he should perform the fire-bath,
naradapuran:78:240	consecrating it with Om eight times, or with the five-syllable mantra, or with any name.
naradapuran:78:241	Holding kusha, he should take ash consecrated seven times. Saying Ishanah sarvavidyanam", he should apply it to the head;
with "Tatpurushaya vidmahe" he should apply ash to the face; with "Aghorebhyo 'tha ghorebhyah" he should put ash on the chest;
with "Vamadevaya namah" on the secret place; with "Sadyojatam prapadyami" he should apply it on the feet;
the wise should dust the whole body with Om. This is the best rule of bathing and so on told for the three twice-born classes.
For Shudras and others I shall tell what the teacher said: having uttered the word "Shiva", the wise one should consecrate the ash.
Taking it seven times, "Shivaya" on the head; "Shankaraya" on the face; "Sarvajnaya" he should put on the heart;
saying "Sthanave namah" on the mouth, "Svayambhuve" he should put on the feet; after that, the ash is pure.
By saying "Namah Shivaya", the dusting of the whole body is remembered. Having washed his hands and sipped water, holding kusha, attentive —
in absence of kusha, gold; in absence of that, sand; in absence of that, durva; in absence of that, silver.
Having done the twilight worship and chanted the Goddess's mantra, he should go to the god's house; or to the god's platform, or a prepared sacrificial ground,
of clay prepared pure, with lotus and other designs, made by the four colours' powders or by white alone,
various lotuses, svastika and so on, lilies, mace, conch, trident and drum,
the five palaces as told, the Shiva-linga, the tree giving all desires, a pot and a bowl,
six-cornered, triangle or nine-cornered; in the corner the twelve ... palanquin, sandals and fans,
a pair of chowries and umbrellas, Vishnu, Brahma and the rest; the wise man should arrange these with powders on the platform or in the temple.
Wherever the god's worship is done, the wise should arrange it so. That made with one's own hand is best; bought, middling;
begged is the lowest, by force the worst. What is taken by force from the worthy or unworthy is fruitless.
With red shali rice, jap... stone-rice, black-gram, red rice, grains of paddy only, in order,
best, middling, low and lowest, by setting the lotus and others, he should perform the sacrifice rightly.
Facing east and north or east, I shall tell the seat as seen and as heard:
of kusha, skin, a cloth bed, wood, palm leaf, wool, gold, silver, copper,
or he should arrange a seat of cow-ear (grass) or arka. Tiger skin, ruru deer, black antelope,
skin is to be known fourfold, and also bandhuka. As possible he should arrange a seat of these.
Having taken the lotus posture or the svastika posture, seated on kusha and ash, controlling breath and speech,
by so doing he becomes of the form of the deity and should meditate within: at the top of the tuft, twelve finger-breadths above, the subtle-bodied Shiva,
moving within beings, in the cave, facing all directions, adorned with all ornaments, endowed with the qualities beginning with "anima" —
having meditated on him, he should hold him in the mind and fill the body with his radiance. By that radiance the sin in the body is destroyed.
As red turns white without contact with gold feet, that twelve-petalled circle, or eight, or five, or three —
having arranged a pure seat and placed the linga there, he should contemplate the great Lord abiding in the cave as the Lord of the linga.
In a purified pot, the water purified and perfumed, putting in sweet-smelling flowers, consecrated with Om,
pranayama and Om are not prescribed for Shudras. In place of pranayama, meditation consecrated with "Shiva" and Om.
Whatever worship-materials there are — perfume, flowers, rice-grains and the rest — having placed them near, he should then make the resolve:
I shall do the worship of Shiva for Shiva's satisfaction. Having so resolved, then invocation and the rest,
up to the bath, he should then perform the bath, with the mantra "Namaste..." according to the Shatarudriya rule.
The unbroken stream is called the stream of liberation. He who bathes (the linga) with it, with chanting and the Rudra head-portions...
once, three, five, seven or nine times, or eleven, or in eleven ways —
this should be known as the bath of liberation, giving liberation in a month. The bath by the Shaiva knowledge or by Om alone,
with clay vessels, coconut pieces, and waves, bell-metal, pearl-shell, or flower filaments —
he should bathe the God of gods with the stated as possible. I shall tell the rule of the horn, how it becomes fit for bathing:
first cleaning inside, then cleaning the outside, making it very smooth and light; he should never cut its limb.
With a spout set in a low one-place channel, with a friendly arrangement, a bath joined with fire he should prepare for the god.
Thus the filling of a gayal's horn with water is told: with a door, with forbidden half-iron, with joint and door joined,
he should arrange a curved snake-staff in snake-form; in the place of the fruit, a cup with a staff having a hole of the same size.
There he should pour the water, set in a pot with a head-machine; he should pour with another or with the left hand.
By this the stream of liberation is made, holy, destroying sin. Having thus bathed the God with the five cow-products,
with the five nectars, and with the three sweet things, having adorned the God with ornaments, he should bathe Maheshvara again.
Having done the cooling services, then rinsing and so on, cloth, sacred thread and perfume materials,
camphor, aloe or patira; he should worship the Shiva-linga with a mixture of both; the whole seat full of perfume, or according to means, silently the services or Kali flowers.
Giving up the unsuitable according to ability, various incense materials or guggulu alone,
all incense mixed with ghee of a tawny cow is praised. Having given incense as able, lamps with tawny cow ghee,
or merely by worship giving lamps and offerings; having given the offering with flowers,
then making mouth-purification, giving betel respectfully, circumambulation and salutation: thus the worship is completed.
Then the five items of song and the like — I shall tell you them: song, instrument, Purana, dance, joking speech,
waving of lights, handful of flowers, offering of all, asking forgiveness and the dismissal — these five services are declared.
Ornament and umbrella, chowries and fans, sacred thread and service: sixteen services.
He who worships Shiva with thirty-two services — by one day all his sins are destroyed."
Hearing Hanuman's words, Shankara said: "So it is, best of monkeys, as you have said about my worship.
I shall now teach you the essence: the worship as in the linga has been told by you at length.
Having worshipped my feet, obtain the fruit of worship." Then the best of monkeys said to the God of gods, Uma's lord:
Worship of the linga is fixed by the teacher. I do it first, O God, and afterward worship your feet.
Having said so, bowing to the Lord, for worship of the Shiva-linga he came to the lake shore and made a sandy platform.
He arranged a seat made of palm leaves. Having washed his feet and hands and sipped water, attentive,
he did the ash-bath, and again sipped water, silent. He made on the god's platform a charming lotus.
Then the monkey, seated on the palm-leaf in the lotus posture, controlling breath, placing, absorbed in pure meditation,
bowed to the teacher, Ishana, and sat chanting. Then the monkey made effort to worship the God.
Placing on the head in the water-pot the pure water brought in two folds of palasha leaf, consecrated by fire,
having done the invocation and so on up to the bath, then taking the god in his cupped hands to bathe him,
the monkey looked and did not see the god's seat. Seeing only the linga in his hand, he became afraid.
The great yogi said this: "What sin have I done, that this Shiva-linga in my hand has no seat?
My death today is certain; the seat will not come. Then I shall chant Rudra; then Maheshvara will come."
Deciding so in mind, he chanted the Shatarudriya. When Maheshvara did not come, the Lord of monkeys
cast down Rudra to the earth; Virabhadra came. "Why are you weeping, good one? Tell the cause of the weeping."
Hearing that, Hanuman said to Virabhadra what was in his mind: "Look at this linga without a seat — see my heap of sin."
Hearing what the monkey said, Virabhadra said: "If the seat does not come to your linga, do not do anything rash.
If the seat does not come, I shall burn the worlds. See, show me whether the seat has come to the linga here or not."
Then, seeing that the seat had not come to the linga, the mighty Virabhadra, wishing to burn all the worlds,
cast fire on the earth; in a moment the earth was burned. Then, having burned the seven lower worlds, it rose upward.
It burned the five upper worlds up to Janaloka's dwellers. Taking with his nail the fire born of his forehead eye,
making it like a citron in his palm, the Lord, lord of sages, set about burning Tapas-loka and Satya-loka.
Then the sages dwelling in Tapoloka, seeing Virabhadra wishing to burn, came to Gautama's hermitage.
Not seeing the Lord Shankara there, abiding in himself, they praised him with devotion with hymns arising from the Veda:

Om — to the God known by the Veda, of pure splendour and inconceivable form, to him — to the Lord of Brahma and the rest, maker of creation and the rest, dear to Vishnu, remover of affliction, maker of the end —
naradapuran:78:323	homage to you, Lord of all, whose garment is space; homage to you pervading the moving and unmoving; homage to the secret of the Veda, fond of devotees; homage to you, lord of sacrifice, who enjoys the offering.
naradapuran:78:324	Homage to you, Shiva, the first God; homage, with the Tortoise; to the bearer of the serpent sacred thread; homage to the one who rains drops of ambrosia, the form of the three Vedas, the Time of Time, O Lord —
naradapuran:78:325	to the bearer of the eightfold form made of earth, wind, space, water, moon, fire, the circle of radiance; to Shiva, destroyer of the inauspicious, the hero: may the Lord of the world always be gracious to us.
naradapuran:78:326	To the moon-browed one; the Self, the great Self, the mind's foremost vehicle, not to be described by words; destroyer of the world's dullness, giver of enjoyment and liberation, may he be gracious always, of pure fame.
naradapuran:78:327	From whom the world was born, by whom it stands protected, in whom it will dissolve, far beyond speech: may he, the Self of the three times, be gracious to us.
naradapuran:78:328	Whose beginning, middle and end none know, not even the wise by their inferences: may he, the universal form, always be gracious to us for our prosperity — what can we tell him here to do?
Hearing this hymn, Shiva, giver of Bhaga's eyes, said to Vishnu: "Bring these sages to me."
Then Vishnu came, comforted the sages dwelling in Tapoloka, and showed them Shankara, Lord of the universe.
Shankara said to them: "For what reason have you come from Tapoloka to the world of earth, sages free of stain?"
Hearing the trident-bearer's words, the best of sages said: "O God, the twelve worlds are seen as heaps of ash.
Only this forest stands; see the destruction of those worlds." Hearing that, Girisha said to those sages of upward-flowing seed:

In the burning of the earth-world and of the nether worlds, sages, there is no doubt; but for us who stand in the secret place,
naradapuran:78:335	there is doubt about the burning of the five upper worlds. How is there a rain of embers? How is there not a great noise?
Hearing the Lord Shankara's words, the lords of sages, with folded hands, said to the God, accompanied by Brahma and the gods:
Fear is on us now from Virabhadra. He himself, thirsty, drank the rain of embers of the Lord.
Then the God summoned the hero and said, "Why, hero?" The hero said: "This was done because the monkey's linga had no seat."
Hearing that, Shiva said to the sages overcome with fear: "This was done by me, O Brahmins, to know the monkey's mind.
Do not fear; I shall always bring about your happiness." Having said so, the God of gods, treasury of mercy, as before,
made all the worlds, even those burned, more beautiful than before, the Lord, Soul of the universe; and said to Virabhadra:
Well done, child, since you always seek the good of devotees; so you will have vast and lasting fame in the world.
Having said so, Maheshvara embraced him, smelled his head, and gave Virabhadra betel with a pleased mind.
Then Hanuman completed the worship as he should; and when the worship was done, Hanuman, glad in mind,
saw there a forest-roaming Gandharva with a lute. He said to him, "Give me the lute."
The Gandharva said: "I will not give up the lute; it is dear to me." "It is dear to me too, Gandharva," said the Lord of monkeys, "the lute."
When the Gandharva did not give the dear lute to the monkey, then with a blow of the fist the Gandharva was felled to the ground.
